description: Logs record individual events, metrics aggregate numbers over time for dashboards and alerts, and traces follow one request through every service as a tree of spans.
The trace id and parent span id each hop forwards to the next, by default in the W3C `traceparent` header, so every span and log line joins the same trace.
The open-source, vendor-neutral standard for producing and exporting traces, metrics and logs: APIs, SDKs, a protocol and a collector, with storage left to a backend.
Latency, traffic, errors and saturation: the minimum to monitor on any user-facing service, with latency read as percentiles.
The measured ratio of good events to all events, the target for that ratio over a window, and the contract with consequences when a target is missed.
1 − SLO over the window: the failures the target tolerates. An error budget policy agreed in advance stops feature releases once it is spent.
A window's error rate divided by the error rate the SLO allows; at 1 the budget lasts exactly the SLO window, at 14.4 one hour spends 2% of a 30-day budget.
A rule that fires only when a long and a short window both exceed a burn rate, such as 14.4 over 1 hour and 5 minutes for a 99.9% SLO.
